question: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating. He was adopted shortly after birth and does not know his biological parents. His pulse is 103/min and blood pressure is 160/105 mm Hg. Physical examination shows multiple soft, yellow papules on the tip of the tongue. There is a 2-cm, firm thyroid nodule. He has long and slender upper extremities, and his elbows and knees can be hyperextended. The most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in which of the following genes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Multiple soft, yellow papules on tongue" -> "Mucosal neuromas" -> "MEN2B syndrome" -> "RET mutation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Firm thyroid nodule" -> "Medullary thyroid carcinoma" -> "RET mutation" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Long and slender upper extremities" -> "Marfanoid habitus" -> "RET mutation" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Hyperextended elbows and knees" -> "Connective tissue abnormality" -> "Marfanoid habitus" -> "RET mutation" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The patient's symptoms and physical findings are consistent with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B), which is associated with a mutation in the RET proto-oncogene. The recurrent episodes of headaches, palpitations, and sweating suggest pheochromocytoma, a common feature of MEN2B. The multiple soft, yellow papules on the tongue are indicative of mucosal neuromas, another hallmark of MEN2B. The firm thyroid nodule is suggestive of medullary thyroid carcinoma, which is also linked to MEN2B. The patient's marfanoid habitus, characterized by long and slender extremities and hyperextensible joints, further supports the diagnosis of MEN2B. The retrieved evidence path confirming the presence of mucosal neuromas on the tongue aligns with the diagnosis. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's condition is a mutation in the RET gene.
